As $P$ increases, the death term dominates $\\\\Delta_{\\\\text{full}}$, and the correlation sharpens because death rates \\\\emph{are} the performance gap. Bootstrap 95\\\\% CIs ($B{=}10{,}000$, seed 42). Full-sample CIs use cluster bootstrap ($K{=}11$); exclusion CIs use episode-level bootstrap over the remaining 10 task types.}\\n\\\\label{tab:daf-sensitivity}\\n\\\\end{table}\\n\\nFor the 10 task types with nonzero death rates, DAF exceeds 97\\\\% across all three model families, confirming that the wider CIs in the full analysis reflect the mechanical effect of including a zero-death task type rather than method instability.\\n\\n\\\\section{Failure Mode Analysis}\\n\\\\label{app:failure-modes}\\n\\nThe most common failure mode for the internal strategy is state hallucination: the model predicts that an action succeeded (e.g., ``the water is now boiling'') when the environment state did not change, leading to cascading errors that trigger agent death.
